output.brief:
The evidence doesn't yet show that store 14's shrink has really risen. The Q1–Q3 figures are interim estimates with an error margin of about ±0.6 points per quarter. The store's total rise is 0.8 points. In past years, about half of the stores that showed two straight rises had them confirmed by the year-end count, and none of the store traits tested predicted which. Store 14's own full-count history is steady at 1.5–1.8%. The shoplifting log is not good evidence of more theft. A new incident app launched chain-wide in April, and recorded incidents rose across the chain while chain shrink stayed flat. The ethics-line tip was checked against CCTV and was innocent: the trips were cardboard bale runs. Sales mix didn't change. Self-checkout and the bus interchange remain unproven. Two neighbouring stores without either show no clear pattern.

What to do: Keep store 14 in the 7 December full count and reject Regional Operations' proposal to drop it, because the count is the only reliable measurement. Don't hire a guard, suspend the stocker, or pull the self-checkout lanes yet. Compare the count with the interim figures. If the rise is confirmed, investigate by department and cause. My confidence is moderate, around 70%.
